### Changelog

* `activeWidgets` could keep widgets that have already been destroyed, so
  `refreshScene` called `align()` with `widget.node === null` (reset by
  `CCObject._destruct`) and threw every frame.
  Entries got in through `visitNode`, which collected widgets by `widget.enabled`

body:
## Summary

Part 2 of #605 — groups the dedup review queue by PROPERTY pair instead of listing pair, with a property-level merge veto so reject binds at the level the UI asks the question. Base is `main` (Part 1 / #610 merged).

#600 measured **892 pending rows collapsing to 669 distinct property-pair questions** — property A with 6 listings and property B with 7 listings produce up to 42 listing-pair rows all asking "is A the same property as B?" identically.

## Two rounds of review, both addressed in full

### Round 1 (design-level): all four blockers + four mediums fixed
Reject was rewritten from an N-request fan-out to a single atomic `reject_pair` action backed by a new `property_merge_veto` table, so rejecting a grouped card actually binds the whole property pair, not just the listing rows the dashboard happened to show.

### Round 2 (targeted re-review of the veto subsystem): confirmed the design and repoint algebra are correct — verified by hand against live Postgres — but found four real problems, all fixed:

**B-1 (blocker) — the repoint test was decorative.** The reviewer deleted the entire repoint step in `perform_merge` and got 18/18 passing — the fixture never actually merged the vetoed property; an unrelated pair supplied `result.merged >= 1`. Rewritten so the vetoed property genuinely LOSES a merge (survivor forced to the other id) and the assertions check the real DB outcome. Added a second test for the collision case (two independent vetoes repointing onto the same pair — `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` must absorb it without an orphan or a UNIQUE violation). Both mutation-checked.

**B-2 (blocker) — "including ones that don't exist yet" was false.** The veto is keyed on property ids. A brand-new listing ingested after the veto starts life as its own new `property` row and isn't covered until it merges onto one of the two vetoed ids — and nothing guarantees it picks the right side (`fetch_listing_records` has no `ORDER BY`, and the #197 same-source skip can make the wrong side the *only* reachable partner in the likely real case). Removed the overclaim from D-133, `init.sql`, `engine.py`, and `dedup-shared.ts`; stated the real guarantee instead (every combination between the two *currently* vetoed ids, including combinations not yet compared). Filed **#612** for the evidence-level-keying fix that gap actually needs — deliberately not bundled into this PR. For the record: on `main` before this PR, that scenario would have auto-merged outright with zero veto protection at all, so this PR is a strict improvement even with #612 open.

**M-1 (promoted to blocker) — a correct veto refusal killed the whole dedup pass.** `_run` had no `try/except` around `perform_merge`, so a genuine mid-run race (a concurrent `reject_pair` action commits a veto between when `_run` loads its in-memory veto set and when it reaches that pair) propagated a `ValueError` out of `engine.run()`, `run_dedup` recorded the run as `failed`, and every pair after that point went uncompared — exactly what happens when the owner taps "Rechazar" on his phone mid-run. Reproduced deterministically with a genuine second Postgres connection (monkeypatched `evaluate_pair` to commit the concurrent veto at the exact right moment — no thread-scheduling luck needed). Now caught at both call sites that can reach `perform_merge`, counted on `DedupRunResult.vetoed_merge_refused`, and the pass continues. `confirm_suggestion`'s own raise is untouched — there it correctly becomes one `failed` action row for one human's one click.

**M-4 — finished the noun pass.** `page.tsx` and the badge tooltip still said "anuncios"; the toggle's "others" count and the badge's total are now shown together in one string ("otros N pares (de M en total)") instead of two separately-labeled numbers a reader has to reconcile, and the e2e fixture moved off N=2 (which never exercised the N vs N−1 relationship) to N=3, with an explicit cross-check assertion (mutation-checked).

**Also taken**: `ps dedup unveto <id> <id>` (M-2 — a veto had no undo path at all, and the repoint step can *widen* a veto onto ids a human never looked at when one of the two vetoed properties later merges into a third); `vetoed_pairs_skipped`/`vetoed_merge_refused` counters printed by `ps dedup run` (M-3 — veto suppression was completely silent before, no counter, no log line, nothing reading the table); the mobile M-2 fixture now seeds a profile match (page-1 guarantee against a real backlog, not just a fresh isolated test DB) and asserts the cancel button actually did something (M-5); the veto table's `property` FKs are `RESTRICT`, not `CASCADE`, matching `property_merge_log`'s own intent (no code path ever actually deletes a `property` row today, and a future purge feature silently discarding a human's veto is exactly the kind of thing that goes unnoticed until it matters).

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run lint` / `npm run typecheck` clean.
- [x] `REQUIRE_DB=1 npm test` — 4361/4361 passing, fresh isolated schema-only database (confirms the new `RESTRICT` FK and schema changes apply cleanly).
- [x] `npm run build` (`next build`) succeeds.
- [x] Python: `etl/tests/test_dedup_engine.py` + `test_dedup_actions.py` — 142/142 passing; full `etl/tests/` suite — 1677/1678 (one pre-existing, unrelated flake in `test_orchestrator.py`'s price-history test — passes in isolation, file untouched by this PR's diff). `ruff format`/`ruff check` clean.
- [x] `scripts/tests/` (decision-id/index-freshness) — 55/55 passing; `DECISIONS.md` regenerated and matches; decision-id allocator re-run immediately before this push, D-133 uncontested.
- [x] e2e (`dedup-review.spec.ts` + `mobile-dedup.spec.ts`, desktop + `devices["iPhone 13"]`) — 11/11 green against a real dev server + fresh throwaway Postgres, including the real confirm/reject round trip via a local Python 3.12 venv running `etl.dedup.cli process-actions`.
- [x] Mutation-checked every new/changed guarantee this round (broke each, confirmed red, restored, confirmed green): the repoint step (both new tests), the mid-run refusal catch (both the direct branch and the reevaluation branch — the mutation also demonstrated `perform_merge`'s own layered defense catching it independently), and the toggle's total/others cross-check assertion.
- No production writes anywhere; no scraped listing content in any commit, test, or fixture.

author: rubicon
body:
## What changed

`oneOf` / `maybeOneOf` beside `req()` in `src/tools.ts`, and every enum-constrained argument routed through one of them. The schema's `enum` and the validator now read the same `const`, so they cannot drift apart.

## Why

`src/index.ts:78` calls a handler with `request.params.arguments ?? {}`. Nothing validates those arguments against the tool's own `inputSchema`, and `req()` only checks presence — so every `enum` in the surface was decoration. A caller could send anything and it went to Forgejo verbatim.

Two cases were worse than a 4xx:

- **`create_pull_request_review.event`** — an unrecognised event doesn't error. Forgejo's `preparePullReviewType` falls through to `ReviewTypePending`, so you get a pending draft *and* a success response. That's the exact silent-success defect fixed in #68, reachable again through the unvalidated path.
- **`merge_pull_request.style`** — elevated and destructive; an unrecognised style should fail here, not be reinterpreted downstream.

`set_issue_state`'s hand-rolled check from #78 is replaced by the shared helper.

## How it was verified

Assertions written first and observed failing. Then mutation-tested:

| Mutation | Caught? |
|---|---|
| drop validation from one field (`list_issues.type`) | yes |
| widen a schema enum without widening its const | yes |
| turn an optional enum required (`maybeOneOf` → `oneOf`) | **no** — until fixed |

That third one is the point of doing this: every merge call in the suite passed a `style`, so an optional enum silently becoming required would have shipped. Added an assertion that an omitted `style` still merges and defaults to `merge`; the mutation now fails with `Missing required argument: style`.

`npm run smoke` and `npm run typecheck` pass. Tool count unchanged at 34.

Closes #79

author: apmantza
body:
## What

The session-state conformance sweep's registered-or-fail coverage claim was
FILE-granular. Once `tests/support/session-state-registry.ts` registered or
exempted a file, the sweep never re-checked what was already inside it — a
NEW module-level `Map`/`Set`/`PathKeyedMap` landing in an already-cleared file
stayed invisible.

`tests/support/sweep-kit.ts` gains `auditSymbolCounts()`, built on the
existing `auditRegistry()` machinery: each flagged file's LIVE
detected-symbol count folds into its registry id (`file@N`), so a file whose
count changes presents an id the pin does not name and reds as an ordinary
unaccounted item. No new registry, no new exemption semantics — the same
machinery, one extra dimension in the id.

`tests/support/session-state-registry.ts` pins `SESSION_STATE_SYMBOL_COUNTS`
— the current detected-symbol count for all 72 files
`scanSessionStateCandidates()` flags today (registered AND exempted). The
conformance suite diffs the pin against a live scan on every run
(`tests/clients/session-state-conformance.test.ts`).

`scanSessionStateCandidates()` (`tests/support/session-state-scan.ts`) now
accepts an optional root override — default behavior and its cache are
unchanged — so the new regression tests can run the real detection logic
against a synthetic fixture tree instead of mutating `clients/` in place.

## Why

Found during #1801's review: `staleGrammarVersionAt`, a process-lifetime
latch on the `TreeSitterClient` singleton, sat unregistered and unreset for a
whole review round while the sweep stayed 55/55 green, because the module
that owns the singleton (`tree-sitter-shared.ts`) was already registered for
an unrelated latch. The file was accounted for; the new symbol inside it was
not.

## Design choice: pinned count vs. full symbol attribution

The issue offered two directions: (a) map every detected stateful symbol to
a reset or a reason, or (b) pin the per-file count so a new one requires a
deliberate update. I chose (b).

(a) would need the registry's `state` field — free text like `"turnCounts,
countedTurnIndex"` — to reliably resolve to the scanner's detected container
identifiers, for all ~30 entries across the registry. It mostly would, but a
few entries name state the scanner cannot see at all (scalars, closures,
class instance fields — `SWEEP_HEURISTIC_LIMITS` documents these as
structural blind spots), so making (a) honest means either fabricating
symbol names for state the scan can't detect, or building a second detector
just to keep the mapping complete. That is a real migration, not a rider on
this fix.

(b) is cheaper and closes the exact gap the issue reports: the AC's
"seeding a new uncleared module-level Map into a registered file reds the
sweep" is satisfied without touching any of the ~30 existing entries. It is
coarser — it says a file's total changed, not which symbol or whether the
new one needs a reset — but it can only ever fail LOUD, never pass silently
on a symbol it never saw.

## Verification

- Red-first: seeded an uncleared `const _probeUnclearedLatch1817 = new
  Map();` into the already-registered `clients/tree-sitter-shared.ts` (the
  #1801 F1 shape exactly), rebuilt, and ran
  `tests/clients/session-state-conformance.test.ts` — the new pin test
  failed: `tree-sitter-shared.ts@1` unaccounted. Reverted the seed (plain
  edit + rebuild, file diff confirmed clean), reran — 61/61 green.
- New regression tests (`session-state sweep — symbol-count pin regression
  (#1817)`) run the real `scanSessionStateCandidates()` detection against a
  synthetic fixture tree, so the #1801 shape stays covered without depending
  on what `clients/` happens to contain: proves file-level coverage alone
  stays clean when a second latch lands (the bug), proves the new pin reds
  on the same fixture, proves it passes when counts match, and proves it
  also reds on a REMOVED symbol whose pin was not updated.
- Targeted suite, all green: `session-state-conformance.test.ts` (61),
  `sweep-kit.test.ts` (mutation-catalogue tests for `auditRegistry`, unchanged
  by this PR), `generation-guard-sweep.test.ts`, `bounded-telemetry-sweep.test.ts`,
  `single-flight-ratchet.test.ts`, `finding-delivery-gate.test.ts` — 6 files,
  193 tests, 0 failed.
- `npm run build` and `npm run lint` (`tsc --project tsconfig.json`) both
  clean.
- Full suite deferred to CI, per repo convention.

## Class sweep

**Pattern**: grepped every consumer of `auditRegistry` in the tree
(`tests/clients/session-state-conformance.test.ts`,
`tests/clients/generation-guard-sweep.test.ts`, plus `sweep-kit.ts`/
`sweep-kit.test.ts` themselves — only two production sweeps are migrated onto
the kit today). `generation-guard-sweep.test.ts` shares the exact defect
shape: `HAND_ROLLED_GENERATION_GUARDS` flags a FILE as hand-rolling a
generation compare, but the check is boolean per file — a SECOND, unrelated
hand-rolled generation compare added to an already-flagged file would not
change the flag and stays invisible. Filing this as a follow-up rather than
folding it into this PR, since the fix's shape may differ (a generation
compare's "identity" is less naturally a count than a session-state
container's).

**Population**: checked the other registered-or-fail sweeps found via
`grep -rl "registered-or-fail\|EXEMPT_\|registered or exempted"`:
`atomic-write-sweep.test.ts` flags per call SITE (line-level), not per file,
so a second write call in an already-covered file gets its own site entry —
not affected. `finding-delivery-gate.test.ts` (#1692) operates at seam/id
granularity via `checkSeamEvidence`, already finer than whole-file — not
affected. `lsp/lsp-fixture-coverage.test.ts` and `bounded-telemetry-scan.ts`
checked and are not file-coverage sweeps of this shape (fixture-file
existence and per-turn admission counters respectively).

## Blast radius

- `auditSymbolCounts()` is new, additive code in `sweep-kit.ts` — no existing
  caller's behavior changes.
- `scanSessionStateCandidates()` gained an optional parameter with a default
  that preserves the exact prior behavior and its module-level cache; every
  existing call site (`session-state-conformance.test.ts`'s five call sites)
  is unchanged.
- No production (`clients/`) code touched. This is test/governance
  infrastructure only.

## Observability

This is a test-time governance gate, not a runtime code path — there is no
production log or ledger record to name. The proof it works is the red run
above: the pin test fails with a named, actionable message
(`tree-sitter-shared.ts@1` unaccounted, plus the remediation string) the
moment a new symbol lands in a registered file.

## Merge order

No open PR touches `tests/support/sweep-kit.ts`,
`tests/support/session-state-registry.ts`,
`tests/support/session-state-scan.ts`, or
`tests/clients/session-state-conformance.test.ts` (checked via `gh pr list`
+ `gh pr diff --name-only` across all currently open PRs). No merge-order
constraint.

Closes #1817.

author: pgillet
body:
Follows the finding in #164 and #166: examples are documentation people copy, nothing imports them, and so they rot silently. `cargo clippy --all-targets` *compiles* the Rust ones but never runs them, and nothing ran the Python ones at all.

**Five were broken at once**, none of it visible in CI.

## The rot

| Example | Failure | Since |
|---|---|---|
| `hurray-ffi/examples/buffer_from_ptr.rs:39` | asserts ABI version `2` | ADR-030 bumped it to 3 (#150) |
| `examples/tensor.py:27` | asserts `not hasattr(t, "__dlpack__")` | DLPack landed |
| `examples/dlpack_numpy.py:32` | `np.from_dlpack(capsule)` — the idiom #166 just removed from the library, still taught here | NumPy 2.1 |
| `examples/native_buffer.py:40` | `hurray.int4` — Tier 2 types live on the `hurray.dtype` submodule | — |
| `examples/display.py:61` | int32 SciPy indices into `from_scipy`, which requires uint64 — the requirement its own cookbook page documents | — |

Two of the fixes are worth calling out because they change what the example *teaches*:

- `tensor.py` now asserts DLPack **is** present, and says why `__array_namespace__` is the one that stays absent (ADR-029: interchange codec, not a compute library). The old line read as though hurray had no DLPack support at all.
- `buffer_from_ptr.rs` asserts against `HURRAY_C_ABI_VERSION` rather than a literal. A literal is guaranteed to go stale on the next ABI bump and says nothing useful when it does.

## The checks

**Python** — `hurray-python/tests/test_examples.py` runs each example as its own parametrized case, so a failure names the file rather than the loop. No workflow edit: CI already runs the whole `tests/` directory, deliberately, so this and any future example are picked up automatically. It also runs locally, which a CI shell loop would not.

**Rust** — a step in the `Test` job runs every example, enumerated from `cargo metadata` so new ones need no edit here either:

```yaml
cargo metadata --format-version 1 --no-deps \
  | jq -r '.packages[] as $p | $p.targets[]
           | select(.kind[] == "example")
           | "\($p.name) \(.name)"' \
  | while read -r pkg example; do
      cargo run -q -p "$pkg" --example "$example" || exit 1
    done
```

Both are **smoke tests**: they assert the script exits zero. That is deliberately not a unit test — these are user-facing narratives, not fine-grained cases. It still checks a good deal, because most examples already assert their own claims: `tensor.py` and `buffer_from_ptr.rs` both failed on an assertion, not an exception.

## Test plan

- [x] All 14 Python examples run clean — `pytest hurray-python/tests/` 134 passed (15 new)
- [x] All 14 Rust examples run clean, via the exact pipeline the CI step uses
- [x] `cargo test --workspace --all-features --exclude hurray-python` — 18 suites green
- [x] `cargo test -p hurray-python` — 145 passed
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

## Cost

The Rust step adds one `cargo run` per example — 14 today, all short, against an already-warm `Swatinem/rust-cache` build in the `Test` job. If that proves too slow it can move to its own job and run in parallel.

author: nesopie
body:
Builds on PR #37 (now merged). This is the half that makes the pre-check *authoritative* and lets the enclave register its own key on-chain.

## What this adds

**RFC-strict signature verification.** The JS verifier now rejects on the RFC's terms rather than mirroring circuit behaviour: leftmost-bit PSS forgeries, off-curve embedded public keys, out-of-range ECDSA scalars, and out-of-range DSC-family pubkey offsets are all `invalid`. Malformed circuit input is reclassified from `skipped` to `invalid` — a shape a genuine document can never have is a rejection, not a coverage gap.

**Two enforcement modes.** `shadow` records a verdict and forwards; `enforce` rejects anything not `valid`. `--precheck-mode=${PRECHECK_MODE:-enforce}` in `start.sh`, with `PRECHECK_MODE` in both Dockerfiles' `allow_env_override` so an operator can drop to shadow with a revision bump rather than an image rebuild.

**Verdict persistence.** `precheck_verdict` / `precheck_reason` on the proofs row, written on every path — including rejections. Since container stdout doesn't leave a Confidential Space instance (`tee-container-log-redirect` is only true for the debug image family), this table is the only observable record of what the pre-check decided.

**The disclose circuits are recognised.** `vc_and_disclose{,_id,_aadhaar,_kyc}` previously fell through to "unknown circuit" → `skipped`, and `enforce` rejects `skipped`. A disclose-feature image would have rejected **every** request; so would the cherrypick image staging runs, which accepts every proof type. Recognition is an exact-match set, deliberately not a `startsWith` — a prefix test would absorb any future `vc_and_disclose_*` circuit into "valid, nothing to check" without anyone deciding that.

**On-chain prover key registration.** Both images now build with `chain`, so the enclave registers its attested key via `registerProverKey` between attestation bootstrap and `server.start`, panicking on failure. It cannot serve a request before its key is registered.

Its rpc url, hub address and submitter key come from Secret Manager under one prefix (`<prefix>RPC_URL`, `<prefix>HUB_ADDRESS`, `<prefix>TEE_PRIVATE_KEY`), never from instance metadata — metadata is readable by anyone with `compute.instances.get`, the submitter key is funded, and a provider rpc url routinely embeds an API key. Only `PROVER_SECRET_PREFIX` travels as metadata, and it names secrets rather than containing any.

## Deploy requirements

This changes what an image needs at boot. Before deploying:

1. **`self-terraform#51`** must land — it supplies `tee-env-PROVER_SECRET_PREFIX`. Without it the enclave panics on startup.
2. **Secrets must exist** for the environment: `staging-PROVER_{RPC_URL,HUB_ADDRESS,TEE_PRIVATE_KEY}`. The first two exist; the key does not yet.
3. **The new image digest** must be added to each secret's IAM (`attribute.image_digest` principalSet) **and** to the prover `PCR0Manager` via `addPCR0`. The current whitelist is pinned to `721f7689…`, which this build supersedes.
4. **The hub must be ≥ v2.14.0** with the four `updateProver…` setters configured, or `registerProverKey` reverts `ProverConfigNotSet` and the enclave crash-loops. Sepolia is on 2.13.0 today.

Registration being fatal at boot is deliberate: an enclave whose key was never registered produces proofs that every register call rejects, so failing to register is failing to serve.

## Tests

| Suite | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Rust (`--features chain`) | **89 passing / 0 failing** |
| JS sidecar | **469 passing / 0 failing**, 0 `not ok` lines |

All 22 non-KYC fixtures still verify. Guards were checked against deliberately broken builds rather than assumed: the disclose near-miss cases fail a prefix-matching implementation, and the blank-input guards fail a build with them removed.

The server commits the outcome before presentation; the reel randomizes its cosmetic start across a full weighted cycle, preserves 2–4 complete cycles, varies cadence and duration, and lands the committed panel under the fixed pointer.
- Derives and validates a seven-cycle rendered strip so every outcome, randomized start, and middle-90% landing keeps the full viewport inside the reel with no trailing blank space.

body:
Fundament für Zuschnitt C. Kein Skript wird hier gegatet — der Wächter und die Ablage der Einmal-Skripte kommen zuerst, damit die Wellen danach gegen eine schrumpfende Liste laufen statt gegen ein Gedächtnis.

## Der Befund, der den Zuschnitt bestimmt hat

Beim Scopen des `reconcile-km-drift`-P1 gemessen:

| Ziel-Gate | Skripte |
|---|---|
| SSoT, zweiteilig (`--confirm-target=host/db`, DB aus offener Connection) | **1** |
| handgeschrieben, **nur Host** | **2** |
| **keins** | **16** |

**18 von 19** schreibenden Skripten waren ungeschützt. Die gehärtete SSoT `server/scripts/lib/prod-write-gate.ts` hatte genau einen Aufrufer. Und die „nur Host"-Form ist die, die am 18.08. gescheitert ist: `helium` heißt in Dev wie Prod gleich.

## Ersetzungs-Regel

| neu | ersetzt |
|---|---|
| `tests/architecture/prod-write-gate-coverage.test.ts` | „jedes Skript denkt selbst daran" |
| gepinnte Altlast-Liste mit Inhalts-Hash | ein Wellenplan, der nur in einem Kopf existiert |
| 4 × `docs/corrections/*.md` | 4 liegengebliebene Einmal-Skripte |

## Warum eine Allowlist — und warum sie nur schrumpfen kann

Ohne sie müssten alle Löcher in einem Zug gestopft werden: ein Groß-PR quer durch Abrechnung, Verschlüsselung und §45b, den niemand ernsthaft reviewen kann. C wäre zu B kollabiert.

Jeder Eintrag trägt den **SHA-256 seines Inhalts**. Das ist der Unterschied zwischen „bekannte Altlast" und „Freibrief":

- Skript **geändert** → Hash passt nicht → rot. Die Liste kann kein Unterstand werden, unter dem ungegateter Code weiterwächst.
- Skript **gegatet** → Test 2 rot → Eintrag muss raus.
- Skript **gelöscht** → Test 1 rot → Eintrag muss raus.

Die Liste schrumpft damit von selbst und kann nicht stillstehen.

## Gegenprobe — alle fünf Umgehungswege

Jede Mutation im Produktivstand, erwarteter Test wird rot:

| | Mutation | fängt |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | neues ungegatetes Skript, nicht gelistet | Hauptregel |
| M2 | dasselbe in die Liste geschmuggelt | Test 4 (Länge + Sortierung) |
| M3 | Altlast-Skript verändert | Test 3 (Hash-Pin) |
| M4 | Altlast-Skript gegatet, Eintrag bleibt | Test 2 |
| M5 | Altlast-Skript gelöscht, Eintrag bleibt | Test 1 |

Bei M5 fielen zunächst **drei** Tests, zwei davon mit `ENOENT`-Stacktrace statt ihrer Meldung — behoben; jetzt zeigt genau einer auf die Ursache. Dazu eine Gegenprobe auf den Wächter selbst: er prüft, dass der Gate-Name in der SSoT wirklich exportiert wird — bei einem Tippfehler wäre sonst jede Datei „ungegatet" oder die Suche liefe ins Leere.

## Was er NICHT kann

Ein Mensch kann einen Eintrag hinzufügen. Verhindern lässt sich das nicht — **sichtbar machen** schon: `BEKANNTE_LOECHER` muss zur Listenlänge passen, jede Ergänzung ändert also die Zahl im Diff, und ein „15 → 16" ist im Review nicht zu übersehen. Stolperdraht, keine Sandbox — dieselbe Ehrlichkeit wie beim `bash-gate`.

## Die vier Einmal-Skripte

Gelöscht und durch Protokolle ersetzt (CLAUDE.md: das Protokoll **ersetzt** das liegengebliebene Skript als Nachweis; der vollständige Nachweis ist git-Historie + DB-Audit-Log + `.md`):

| Skript | Protokoll |
|---|---|
| `migrate-invoice-status-model.ts` (`10db8bf8`) | `2026-08-18_rechnungsstatus-modell.md` |
| `correct-schroeder-39.ts` (`19a43a2f`) | `2026-05-28_schroeder-39-importluecken.md` |
| `fix-ursula-99-june-rebill.ts` (`5b5f82bd`) | `2026-07-23_neuber-99-juni-rebill.md` |
| `cleanup-vavrin-96-budget-phases.ts` (`0d80cb9d`) | `2026-07-16_vavrin-96-budgetphasen.md` |

author: humiley
body:
Three columns on the register — **Scheduled quantity · Actual at site · % Complete** — with the
third computed from the first two, and a **unit of work** (m, m², m³, kg, no., set, lot…) carried on
the line.

## It drives the schedule, it doesn't just display

Quantity → percentage → weighted roll-up → master activity → S-curve, board, variance, Power BI.
Report a quantity at site and the contract programme moves. That's why this lives in the reading
rather than in a column.

## The decision that matters is per reading

A reading carrying a **quantity** is a measurement; one carrying only a **percentage** is an
estimate. The measurement wins where it exists — decided **per reading, not per item**.

Per item would mean a line that gained a quantity halfway through lost every earlier reading: it
would drop to 0% the moment somebody filled the quantity in. That's the worst possible moment to
zero a schedule. Tested in both directions.

## Not every line has a quantity

Mobilisation, testing, a permit — some work genuinely has no measure. Those read *"no quantity —
progress is judged"* and keep the typed percentage. Half measured and half judged is the normal
state of a real programme; the register says which is which rather than implying a rigour it
doesn't have.

## An inferred figure never passes as measured

Where a quantity exists but only a percentage was filed, the site column shows the back-calculated
number in lighter italic with a tooltip saying so — and the BI fact table carries `qtyMeasured=0`
beside it. Summing an inferred quantity as though someone had counted it is precisely the error a
chart makes silently.

## Verified

- **11 new JS assertions** (43 total) + **5 in `tests/test_bi.py`** — deliberately the same cases
  with the same numbers on both sides of the port, so the two implementations can't drift
- Full Python suite green
- In the browser on seeded lines: `2,400/2,400 m = 100%`, `1,128/1,200 m = 94%`, judged lines

## Summary

- Every redirecting route guard now returns a `UrlTree` instead of calling `router.navigate()` and returning `false`, which is what Angular's `CanActivate` contract asks for: the tree cancels the in-flight navigation and starts the redirect in one router cycle, and the destination travels on the `NavigationCancel` event so a denial is distinguishable from a plain "stay put".
- No user-visible defect motivated this and none is claimed. What the old shape cost: two navigation cycles per redirect, a `NavigationCancel` carrying a bare `false`, a discarded navigation promise at every site (a rejected redirect was silent), and guards that could only be tested through a Router spy.
- Scope is six redirect sites, two of them outside `features/auth`. `billingAvailableGuard` was already on the contract, so the redirect shape is now uniform across every guard in the app.

## Changes

**Client - guards**
- `features/auth/utils/ensure-authenticated.ts` - all three login exits (no persisted user, refresh resolved null, refresh threw) return the login tree. Callback and return type widen from `boolean | Observable<boolean>` to Angular's own `GuardResult | Observable<GuardResult>`; `CanActivateFn` already accepts it, so no cast was needed anywhere.
- `features/auth/guards/guest.guard.ts` - both `/profile` redirects.
- `features/auth/guards/permission.guard.ts` - `permissionGuard` and `instancePermissionGuard`.
- `features/admin/guards/admin-panel.guard.ts` and `features/feature-flags/guards/feature-flag.guard.ts` - the two guards outside `features/auth` that compose `ensureAuthenticated`, converted with it rather than left on the old contract.

Both build from the same commands and extras, so the `returnUrl` encoding cannot drift between them.

**Tests**
- Guard specs assert on the returned tree (`expect(String(result)).toBe('/login?returnUrl=%2Fusers')`) rather than on a Router spy - the guards are pure functions of the store now. Where a spy survives it asserts `router.navigate` was **not** called, pinning the contract.
- `ensure-authenticated.spec.ts` swaps its hand-rolled Router stub for a real `provideRouter([])` instance and gains a case for a `UrlTree` returned from the `onAuthenticated` callback.
- `adminPanelGuard` had no spec at all; it gets one (allow / `/forbidden` / `/login?returnUrl=%2Fadmin`).

author: erictheng93
body:
Closes #202.

## The bug

`turbo run test` starts one vitest per package and each of those forks its own workers, so the number of live node processes is a **product**:

```
(turbo concurrency) x (workers per package)
```

Neither factor was bounded. vitest picks `max(availableParallelism() - 1, 1)` — 23 on a 24-core box, 3 on a 4-core one — and turbo's default concurrency is 10.

## Measurements

All on a 24-core / 15.9 GB Windows host, this tree.

| | peak `node.exe` |
| --- | --- |
| `apps/kitchen-display` alone, no ceiling | **26** |
| `apps/kitchen-display` alone, `--maxWorkers=2` | 5 |
| 3 jsdom packages, `--concurrency=3`, `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=23` | **61** |
| 3 jsdom packages, `--concurrency=3`, ceiling active | 18 |
| full `turbo run test --force --continue`, ceiling active | **39** |

Full run after the fix: **24/24 tasks, 499 test files, 0 failures, 3m53s.**

The ~260 figure for a full unbounded run is arithmetic from the measured 26-per-package, not a measurement — deliberately not reproduced, since 260 node processes against 15.9 GB would have thrashed the machine.

## What changed

- **`vitest.shared.ts`** (new) holds the ceiling; all 17 per-package `vitest.config.ts` spread it. It cannot live in the root `vitest.config.ts` — a per-package vitest invocation reads that package's own config as its root and never sees the root file.
- **`scripts/verify.sh`** caps the other factor at half the cores, overridable via `TURBO_CONCURRENCY`. Bounding one factor alone is not enough; #202 recorded `--concurrency=2` by itself still running out of memory.
- **`turbo.json`** — two entries that each hide a trap:
  - `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS` in `globalPassThroughEnv`: turbo's strict env mode was silently dropping it, so the override *looked* like it worked while doing nothing. Caught by an A/B that measured 18 vs 18 instead of 61 vs 18.
  - `vitest.shared.ts` in `globalDependencies`: it sits outside every package's `$TURBO_DEFAULT$` inputs, so without it a changed ceiling returns a stale cache HIT.
- **`scripts/check-package-test-scripts.cjs`** grows a fifth rule: a `vitest.config.*` that omits the spread fails the build. Negative-tested.
- **`apps/customer-app/tsconfig.json`** — its `include` has `*.config.*` and the project is `composite`, so the new import needed listing (TS6307). No other composite project includes its config files.

## Corrections to the issue as filed

author: myagentdojo
body:
Found while testing whether development mode overrides a production install. It
does not override it — it **replaces** it — but the preview never said so.

## The gap

`install --apply` issues these against the user profile:

```
claude plugin uninstall <name>@<name> --keep-data --scope user
claude plugin marketplace remove <name> --scope user
claude plugin marketplace add <checkout>/.dev/claude/marketplace --scope user
claude plugin install <name>@<name>-dev --scope user --yes
```

The preview before that read:

> Review the captured production state, then rerun with `--apply`.

The same sentence whether or not a production installation existed. It asked for
consent to an action it never named, and pointed at a "captured production
state" the reader had no way to see.

`sideEffects` was not the place to fix it: entries there are pushed **after**
each mutation succeeds, so a planned action listed there would misreport the
profile as already changed.

## After

With a production installation present:

> `--apply` will uninstall `my-second-brain@my-second-brain` with `--keep-data`
> and remove the `my-second-brain` Marketplace, then install development mode.
> `bun run dev -- claude restore` puts the production state back. Review this,
> then rerun with `--apply`.

With none:

> Review the planned development installation, then rerun with `--apply`.

It names the plugin id, the `--keep-data` flag that makes the replacement
recoverable, the Marketplace removal, and `restore` as the exit — and stays
quiet about a replacement that will not happen.

## Proof

Two tests, written before the change and confirmed to fail against the old fixed
string:

- preview with production present names the uninstall, the id, and `--keep-data`
- preview with production absent claims no replacement

The existing test that the preview mutates nothing still passes, so this adds
disclosure without adding a side effect.

- Full suite: **756 pass, 10 skip, 0 fail**
- `generate:check` current

## Not changed

The refusal behaviour is already correct and stays as it is: coexistence raises
`DUPLICATE_PLUGIN_SOURCES`, and `install` refuses up front with
`PRODUCTION_SOURCE_UNRESTORABLE` when the production Marketplace source could
not be reconstructed — verified to issue zero commands in that case.

body:
Carries the review findings from #376. (#378 was the first attempt at this and merged **empty** — 0 files, +0/-0 — after its branch was accidentally force-pushed to main's tip while auto-merge was armed. Same commit, clean branch.)

## The SA5011 exclusion was carrying its own expiry date

`.golangci.yml` excluded SA5011 from `_test.go` with this reason:

> this staticcheck build (golangci-lint 2.12.2, built with go1.26.2) does not recognise `t.Fatal` as no-return... **Revisit when golangci-lint is rebuilt on the running toolchain.**

#376's bump to v2.13.0 (built with go1.26.6) is precisely that trigger, and it didn't revisit. This does.

**Dead, not merely unexercised.** The distinction matters, because "0 issues after removing an exclusion" normally proves only that nothing currently trips it. Here the comment states the false positive hit *every* guard of that shape, and the tree holds **403** `if x == nil { t.Fatal(...) }` guards in test files. With the exclusion removed the linter reports **0 issues on the darwin tree and 0 on the linux tree**. A live false-positive class would have produced hundreds; zero is therefore evidence, not absence of evidence.

Removing it restores real SA5011 coverage over test files, which the exclusion had been silently withholding since the analyser caught up.

## Parser hardening

#376's ci.yml version parser stopped only at whitespace, so a trailing comment written without a preceding space — `GOLANGCI_LINT_VERSION: v2.13.0# pinned` — yielded `"2.13.0#"`. That is a **wrong** value, which warns even when the versions genuinely match; an empty one would merely skip the check. The character class now stops at `#` as well.

Verified against six shapes: plain, `#comment` with and without a preceding space, no `v` prefix, a prerelease suffix (`v2.13.0-rc1`), and a comment line that mentions the variable (correctly empty, so the guard skips rather than misfires).

## Stale version references

Two doc comments in `internal/quality/golangcilint` named v2.12.2 as the version a behaviour was *measured* at. The measurement still holds — the integration test passes against the real v2.13.0 binary — so `analyser.go` records that it was **re-confirmed** at v2.13.0 rather than silently restating the old figure, and the test's own prose drops a version it never needed to name. Rewriting the number outright would have misrepresented what was actually measured.

## Verification

- `make verify` green; `make lint-cross` reports the **linux** tree clean.
- The SA5011 experiment ran with an isolated `GOLANGCI_LINT_CACHE`, after observing cross-worktree cache collisions on this machine.
- `go test -tags=integration ./internal/quality/golangcilint/ -run PathPrefixDoesNotSurviveAbsPathMode` passes against v2.13.0.

## Solde de la revue U1-f — les six findings P2 confirmés

La revue adversariale du lot précédent avait confirmé quatorze findings. Les deux P0 et les P1 ont été traités dans la PR #99 ; **cette PR solde les six P2 restants**, pour ne rien laisser derrière.

**Le reçu d'effet est redevenu idempotent.** La description de l'effet réussi relisait la révision *courante* de la fiche à chaque redelivery. Or cette révision sert au domaine à reconnaître un **rejeu** — un second reçu identique est un no-op. Une écriture survenue entre-temps (l'artisan corrige sa fiche) donnait une révision différente, et le rejeu cessait d'être reconnu comme tel. Quand le run porte déjà le reçu de cet effet, il fait désormais foi : on le rend à l'octet.

**Bob ne promet plus ce qu'il refuse.** En attente de confirmation sur une *modification*, la voix annonçait la capacité `confirm` puis la refusait systématiquement — une modification se confirme à l'écran (§7.0 règle 3). L'artisan pouvait répéter « je confirme » sans que rien n'arrive. L'outil n'est plus offert ; l'assertion est greffée sur le test qui prouvait déjà le refus, si bien que les deux faits vivent au même endroit.

**Un commentaire qui mentait.** La migration déclare `resultDigest` inatteignable par l'autorité de dispatch — c'est faux, sa policy en dépend pour la branche de redelivery. Le provisionnement dit maintenant ce qu'il fait, et nomme ce qui reste réellement hors d'atteinte : `payloadRef`, `authorizationSource`, `submittedJobRef`, `targetDigest`, `authorizationDigest`. Un digest de résultat est une empreinte opaque, pas une charge.

**Un échec devenu visible.** La lecture display-only de la fiche était avalée sans aucune trace : le libellé et l'« avant » pouvaient disparaître pour tous les artisans sans que personne ne l'apprenne, et la carte redevenait muette exactement comme avant U1-f.

**La certification prouvait une surface plus large que la réalité.** Il lui manquait deux gestes que `release.sh` exécute : la remise à plat des ACL **par colonne** (un privilège survivant d'un provisionnement antérieur élargirait la surface sans que le GRANT le dise) et la révocation de l'adhésion du rôle applicatif vers l'autorité.

body:
## Summary

Adds the Multi Select core state (Task 7A): a sibling module of Combobox with its own unconditional public contract. The existing Combobox API is untouched; only the internal collection helpers are shared. Out of scope by design: free-form values, token creation, reordering, drag and drop, minimum selection, async fetching, virtualization, styled adapters (7B).

### API (`core/src/multi-select`, exported as `multiSelect`)

- Types: `MultiSelectItem`, `MultiSelectState`, `MultiSelectContext` — `values: string[]` ordered, unique and controlled via `onValuesChange`, default empty; `max`, `disabled`, `readOnly`, `removeOnBackspace` (default `false`).
- Pure transitions with the same-reference no-op convention (a no-op can never reach a setter): `addValue` (duplicate additions and additions past `max` are no-ops; `max` never removes existing values), `removeValue` (every occurrence; absent value is a no-op), `lastRemovableValue` (skips disabled selections), `resolveItem` (a value whose item disappeared stays selected with a raw, safe text fallback).
- `connect` with **required** setters: `select` adds the active option, keeps the popup open for another choice and clears the filter text; reselecting a selected option is a silent no-op; `remove`/`removeLast` respect disabled/readOnly and disabled items; `openListbox` blocked by disabled and readOnly, no pre-highlight (keyboard ArrowDown opens highlighting the first enabled option); Escape closes only while open and never moves focus; Backspace removes only with the explicit opt-in and an empty input.
- Semantics: labelled `role="combobox"` input with `aria-activedescendant`, `aria-multiselectable="true"` listbox, `aria-selected` reflected on every option (selected options stay listed and reviewable), `aria-disabled`/`readonly`, `data-*` hooks, and the selected-values list container id (tags never get option semantics). Remove-button labels, hidden form inputs and `aria-required` passthrough are adapter work (7B); native `required` constraint validation is documented out of scope.

### Tests

- 24 unit tests: controlled reflection, uniqueness and order (including hostile duplicated input), max at/over the cap without pruning, disabled/readOnly gating with review intact, disappearing-item retention, navigation skipping disabled options, Enter-keeps-open, Escape semantics, the full Backspace policy, ARIA wiring, and spy proof that no-op paths never reach any setter.
- Node import test (`@vitest-environment node`); the packed-consumer smoke now imports `multiSelect` and asserts runtime and type resolution.

## Testing

- `pnpm test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm api:check`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm size`, `pnpm audit`, `core run smoke`: all green.
- Mutation checks applied and reverted (reselect toggling, max off-by-one, Backspace removing disabled values, select closing the popup, addition losing order): each caught by failing tests.

body: ## Summary Implements the `operator-portal` module at `/commercial/operator-portal`: the view an airline customer sees of its own fleet — engine status, planned removals, AOG, contract performance, and the decisions Rolls-Royce needs back from them this week. Everything is derived from `@rr/data`; no display rows are hardcoded. The new selector layer produces a **customer-safe projection** — the `OperatorPortalView` types deliberately have no fields for cost, margin, penalties or rates, so internal commercial data cannot leak into this page or the API route by construction. ```ts // packages/data/src/modules/operator-portal.ts listOperatorPortalOptions(): OperatorPortalOption[] // switcher, with per-operator open-action counts buildOperatorActions(operatorId): OperatorAction[] // "what we need from you", red → amber → due date, capped at 12 buildOperatorPortalView(operatorId): OperatorPortalView | undefined ``` Actions are unioned from five domain sources rather than a single table: planned/draft work orders (schedule slot confirmation), awaiting-parts work orders (lease/AOG decision), critical & high alerts still `new`/`triaged`, mandatory service bulletins, and amber/red LLP statuses. Each carries a `reason` and a `recommendedAction`, so every red row on the page answers "why is this red?" inline. Page is a server component; `"use client"` is limited to the action list (category filter + local accept/query state) and the fleet tabs (search + sort). The operator switcher is server-rendered links driving `?operator=`. API (additive, one responsibility each): ``` GET /operator-portal/operators → OperatorPortalOption[] GET /operator-portal/:operatorId → OperatorPortalView (404 in the existing error shape) ``` Shared-file edits are limited to the three allowed by `AGENTS.md`: the `operator-portal` `implemented` flag, one barrel export line in each of `packages/{types,data}/src/modules/index.ts`, and one registration line in `apps/api/src/routes/modules.ts`. ### Domain assumptions - "Availability" is contractual aircraft availability vs. the contract target; dispatch reliability is a 30-day rolling figure. Rebuilds the Activity page presentation to match the updated design frame: [Activity 13164:77644](https://www.figma.com/design/NgDfn7fVnkQZP0XH9Uki63/TBV-v.3--Premium-Design-?node-id=13164-77644).

Stacked on `feat/activity-usd-and-live-status` (#2114 + #2116). It reuses that branch's `ActivityAmount.numeric` plumbing and its `usePrices` / `useVaults` wiring rather than adding its own.

## What changed

| Aspect | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Toolbar | "Show all" dropdown at the left | Search box at the left ("Search tx hash or type of transaction"), "Show All" dropdown pinned right |
| Date groups | Today / Yesterday / `YYYY-MM-DD` | Today / Yesterday / **Last week** (2–7 days back) / `YYYY-MM-DD` beyond that |
| Row anatomy | icon + amount, status dot + label, type, hash, time | icon, **type as the primary label with the asset symbol beneath it**, labelled explorer link, labelled timestamp, **right-aligned amount with its USD sub-line** |
| Status | Dot + "Done" / "In use" / "Expired" / "Pending" column | **Column removed.** Pending spins a 16px loader beside the type label; a refunded deposit gets a "Refund" chip and its card loses its fill while the row fades to 60% |
| Liquidation card | Child rows carried a repeated status dot | Same card, children now read "Liquidated" / "Debt repaid" and each carries its own USD sub-line |

Search filters the rows already loaded — transaction hash (with or without `0x`) and the visible type text, debounced at 200ms. No new indexer query. The type filter keeps its behaviour; only its styling and position changed.

## Decisions worth a look

**The explorer label is derived, not hardcoded.** The frame draws "Xangle Explorer :", but this cell links through `getExplorerTxUrl`, which points at mempool.space for BTC rows and the configured chain explorer for ETH rows — never the VP explorer that `NEXT_PUBLIC_TBV_VP_EXPLORER_URL` configures. The label is derived from the host actually linked ("Mempool", "Etherscan"), so it follows the environment instead of claiming an explorer the link never opens. Flagging for design: if the intent was to link the Babylon vault explorer instead, that is a different link, not a different label.

**"In use" has no surface in this design, and that is a question for design.** #2116 makes a deposit row's status reflect live vault state; this frame removes the status column entirely, so nothing renders that distinction any more. Per the brief the derivation stays wired — `useVaults` → `activeVaultIds` still flows from the container through the list into the row's props — but no component reads it, and the label rendering plus its tests are removed here (there is no longer a label for those tests to assert). **If depositors should still be able to tell a deposit whose collateral is in use from one that has been withdrawn or redeemed, the design needs a surface for it.** Re-rendering it is a small change once that surface exists.

**Row dimming is one opacity, not a recoloured palette.** The frame recolours every text run in a dimmed row to `text/tertiary`. This applies `opacity-60` to the row and drops the card fill instead — one class, and it holds in dark mode, where a hardcoded `#b0b0b0` would not.

## What the frame draws that the data cannot back yet

Listed as follow-ups, not implemented here:

- **"Failed" chip + dimmed row.** `ActivityLog` has no failure state — the indexer projection cannot emit a failed row today. The chip treatment is built (the refunded-deposit path uses it) and would only need the projection to mark a row as failed.
- **"Fairness Payment" rows.** No such event reaches the activity projection. The frame draws it as a third liquidation child.
- **"Debt repaid" as a standalone row.** It exists only as a liquidation child, which is how it renders here.

Also worth noting: the refunded ("Refund" chip) row still carries its Withdraw action when the HTLC refund is outstanding. The frame draws no action on that row, but dropping the button would remove the only way to reclaim those funds.

## Testing

- Extended the existing Activity suites in place: group labels including "Last week" and the future-date guard, the new row anatomy, search filtering (hash, type text, empty result, debounce), the refund chip and row dimming, the pending spinner, and the liquidation card's per-child pricing.
- New: `activitySearch.test.ts` for the matcher, `LiquidationGroupCardV3.test.tsx` for the group card.
- The base branch's In use / Done row tests are removed with the label they asserted; its USD tests are kept as-is.
- `tsc --noEmit`, ESLint on every touched path, and the full vault suite: **3412 passed, 6 skipped, 0 failures**.

Verified against the live frame. No dark twin was located next to it; the implementation uses the app's semantic colour tokens throughout, which theme automatically.

author: robertinoc
body:
## The gap

Gig Mode showed the clock time each track was **due** at. It never compared that to the **actual** time — which is the comparison a booth screen exists for.

A DJ twenty minutes behind with six tracks left needs to cut two of them *now*, while there's still a choice about which two. At 02:58 the choice has been made for them.

## What it reports

`assessPace` → drift, slot remaining, tracks remaining, and **minutes per remaining track** — the last being the one that turns drift into a decision. *"25min left for 6 tracks — about 4 min each"* is actionable in a way that *"25 minutes behind"* isn't.

## The load-bearing part

`locateInSlot`, and it exists because **most club slots cross midnight** while both values are minutes-from-midnight:

> At 00:30 in a 23:00–01:00 slot, `now − start` is **−1350** — which reads as twenty-two hours early when the truth is ninety minutes in.

Modular arithmetic fixes that and introduces its own ambiguity: every instant is simultaneously a little *before* the slot and a lot *after* it. So the two candidate distances are compared and the nearer one wins. 22:30 is 30 minutes early, not 22.5 hours late; 01:30 is 30 minutes late, not 21.5 hours early. Both directions have tests, as does the non-wrapping slot so the general case can't regress.

## Three deliberate restraints

- **Null before the slot starts.** Telling a DJ they're "ahead of schedule" an hour before they go on is noise dressed as information.
- **`useNowMinutes` is null through hydration.** Reading the clock during render would make server and client markup disagree, and a hydration mismatch on the one screen someone opens mid-set isn't worth half a second of earliness. Ticks every 30s — a minute would let the drift sit a full minute stale, faster just spends battery.
- **The copy states a fact and its consequence, never an instruction.** Whether to cut two tracks or ride a long mix is the DJ's call, and a booth screen that tells someone what to play is the fastest way to get itself ignored.

Colour-coded (amber behind, sky ahead, dim on-time) and placed above "now playing" — the second thing the eye lands on, because it's the only line there that can change what happens next.

## Verification

`tsc --noEmit` · `vitest run` → **1000 passed** (15 new in `slot-pace.test.ts`) · `eslint .` · `next build`

author: plantucha
body:
`PPGDEX-JITTER-AND-REFERENCE-FOLLOWUPS` §6.8 names the test that settles the 8.36-vs-5.92 question:

> *"re-run the wrist leg on the **ORIGINAL 15-night set** with the match rate beside it (that corpus is not on this volume)"*

**The match rate is already recorded** — in the sibling brief that produced 8.36, `O2RING-FINGER-HRV-VALIDATION` §8.1:

| | nights | PPI-jitter sd (median) | IQR | beat match rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Verity WRIST** | 15 | **8.36 ms** | **4.63 – 31.61** | **100 % (IQR 86.7–100)** |

## Neither branch of the test fits

It offers *"8.4 with a **low** match rate ⇒ night quality"* or *"5 with a **high** one ⇒ apparatus"*. The actual pair is **8.4 with a 100 % match rate** — which the framing didn't anticipate, so no corpus re-run resolves it as posed.

## And the discrepancy isn't statistically present

That IQR spans **4.63 – 31.61 ms**, and **5.92 sits inside it**. *"8.36 ms: 41 % higher"* compares a median against a point value with the spread discarded, on a distribution ~27 ms wide. §8.2's own honest line — *"I cannot attribute it"* — was written directly beneath the IQR showing there is little to attribute. §1's re-run (median **6.09**, IQR 4.57–7.54) is consistent with both figures for the same reason.

⚠️ This is also why §6.8's 4-night IQR (**4.92–5.03**) must not be read as the *tighter* measurement — it's the spread of **four** numbers against fifteen. §6.8 already warns about exactly this, and the warning applies to the comparison the section then invites.

## The transfer buys precision, not a verdict

Recorded for whoever wants it: the box holds **26 nights** carrying both Verity PPG and H10 ECG under `/srv/tepna/captures` (27 total), **13 GB** of paired files — more than the 15 the test names.

But **the original fifteen are not identified anywhere**, so a 26-night run produces a **fourth** number for this quantity rather than adjudicating the existing three. Naming the nights is the prerequisite, not the transfer — which is why I checked the box's contents but did not copy anything.

**What remains genuinely open** is narrower than the section implies: not *which figure is right* — they aren't distinguishable at the recorded precision — but *what the wrist's PPI jitter is with an interval anyone can quote*. The 15-night IQR says the current answer is not that.

## Gates

Docs-only — no code, no bundle, no changeset. `docs-ledger` **38 green**.

author: akiyama-mizuki-44
body:
## Summary

- introduce typed, immutable `Event` records with explicit event types and propagation scopes
- add an ordered, append-only `EventStore` as authoritative world history
- add an atomic commit boundary for applying WorldState changes and recording events
- commit accepted dialogue as events linked to their generation `Turn`
- project existing WebSocket turn messages from committed events while preserving compatibility
- document Event and committed world-history semantics

## Event model

Initial scopes:

- private
- participant
- channel
- location
- public / ambient

Initial event types:

- `dialogue.spoken`
- `message.sent`
- `presence.joined_channel`
- `presence.left_channel`
- `world.time_advanced`
- `character.location_changed`

Event payload and provenance data are deep-frozen after construction. Public serialization returns independent mutable copies.

## Commit semantics

The commit boundary:

1. validates event shape, references, timestamp, scope, and state-transition preconditions
2. snapshots mutable session/world state
3. applies the event’s declared state effect
4. appends the event to ordered world history
5. records the corresponding Turn when applicable
6. rolls everything back if any step fails

This prevents partial states such as:

- world changed without an event
- event recorded without its state effect
- dialogue event recorded without its Turn
- Turn recorded without its dialogue event

## Integrity safeguards

- reject duplicate event IDs and backward timestamps
- require event time to match the authoritative WorldState clock
- reject unknown characters, locations, channels, and participants
- reject duplicate channel joins, invalid channel leaves, and no-op location changes
- keep EventStore’s public surface read-only
- validate serialized sequence numbers during restoration
- prevent rejected or failed generation attempts from entering world history
- preserve the existing `error` + `done` WebSocket lifecycle for unexpected commit failures

## Compatibility

- existing deterministic research sessions remain available
- existing turn fields remain unchanged
- turn messages gain an additional `event_id` linking them to world history
- drift JSONL and Markdown history remain compatible projections
- OOC results still represent dialogue that occurred; Router queues correction but does not retroactively erase the event
- Exposure, Agency, Memory, and persistent scheduling are intentionally not included

## Testing

```text
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests

Ran 178 tests — OK
```

Python compilation and `git diff --check` also pass.

author: xugangqiang
body:
## What

`DedupSubstringOverlaps` could not recognize an OCR paragraph-level box and its contained line-level fragment as a substring pair when the fragment carried char-layer text that preserved the PDF's original spaces.

## Why

`ocrMergeChars` fills OCR line fragments with char-layer text that keeps the PDF's original spaces (`- name: SSL_CERT_FILE`, `⽂章 中 提到`), while the containing paragraph OCR box carries the recognizer's joined text (`-name: SSL_CERT_FILE`, `⽂章中提到`). The byte-wise `strings.Contains` check in `DedupSubstringOverlaps` therefore failed, the inner box survived to `NaiveVerticalMerge`, and the two were concatenated — duplicating content.

On the real_pdfs parity dataset (`BATCH_PARITY_VARIANT=ocr_real`) this surfaced as textSim gaps:
- plugin-daemon: 92.2% → 98.1% (YAML block split into duplicated lines)
- RAG分词召回分析: 96.1% → 98.2%
- broad textSim improvement across the dell/prodeploy/asset-recovery marketing PDF cluster

## How

- `DedupSubstringOverlaps` now compares **whitespace-normalized text** (`dedupNormText` strips all unicode whitespace) while keeping the geometry containment proof (`boxInside`) unchanged. Whitespace is the only divergence between char-derived fragment text and OCR box text; the containment geometry is the actual proof.
- The legacy `len(ai) == len(aj)` skip became `ai == aj`, so whitespace-equal contained fragments (e.g. `-name:` vs `- name:`) also collapse.
- Normalized text is **precomputed once per box** to avoid O(n²·len) recompute on large scan documents (~3k boxes).
- `boxInside` now requires **FULL horizontal containment** (`inner.X0 >= outer.X0 && inner.X1 <= outer.X1`) in addition to Y containment — a box that pokes out to either side is an adjacent-column line, not an OCR fragment, and must not be dropped by a whitespace-normalized substring match (review finding).

## Boundary guards (kept)

- disjoint-Y / different-column substring fragments are kept
- partial-Y-overlap (extends below the container) is kept
- horizontal overhang (extends past the container on either side) is kept
- taller-container fragments are kept
- char-path (IsOCR=false) boxes are never collapsed

## Tests

- 7 new unit tests: whitespace-divergent substring (ASCII + CJK), whitespace-equal contained fragment, horizontal overhang, and the boundary guards above.
- Synthetic 35-PDF parity: `aligned=32 failed=0` (no regression).
- real_pdfs ocr_real parity: no status flip; 15 files improve. The only run-to-run delta (lazards-lcoeplus ±0.2%) is table-HTML noise, not a content regression.

## Remaining gaps (separate issues)

三国人物 / Rag Flow Usage / 刑法 / 1例3个月 text gaps are reading-order and paragraph-granularity differences, not OCR dedup — tracked separately.
